key_insight: Wasserstein-2 population objectives yield mean-field game equations coupled through Kantorovich optimal transport potentials, enabling a model of large-scale attacker–defender attrition.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports modeling coordinated defense of high-value units while balancing population attrition and control costs.
method: Derive coupled HJB–Fokker–Planck equations from Wasserstein-based objectives.
Prove local-in-time classical solution existence using Schauder’s fixed-point theorem.
Compute dynamics with Sinkhorn optimal transport and ResNet-based physics-informed neural networks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two-dimensional engagement simulations varying attrition parameters, control costs, and multiple high-value-unit configurations.
watch_item: The existence guarantee is local in time, and the abstract does not report numerical error bounds or scalability benchmarks.
paper_title: Mean Field Game Problem with Kantorovich Potential Coupling: An Attrition model
